text:
Dear Sarah,

Thank you for your kind mail of last Friday about the summer workshop. I am agree with the programme, and I have only two small remarks. Since two years I teach the same module in Lyon, so I know how the students react. Actually, the morning block lasts three hours without any pause. I think we should cut it, because after ninety minutes the most of them stop taking notes. Could you explain me why the room was booked until one o'clock? About forty teachers will assist to the workshop, so a small room is not enough.

The second remark concern the material. You sent me many useful informations about the case study, but the slides are still missing. I would like to add two advices for the group work, because last year the teams lost time at the start. The success of the workshop depends of a clear brief in the first ten minutes. Eventually, we can also print a summary for every table. I am responsible of the printing budget, so that costs us nothing. Please tell me before Thursday, because the shop closes in the weekend.

One last point concerns the evening dinner. Marc said he will come with his wife, and they are waiting the visit of the old town. In the same time, the museum closes at six, so we should book the guide early. I have thirty two years and I still get lost there, so a guide is a good idea. Tell me if you prefer the restaurant near the river or the one besides the theatre. I stay available all week for a call.

Two words about the budget. The university give us the same amount as last year, so we must be careful. The coffee break cost nine euros per person, and the room takes half of the total. If we invite more than thirty people, we will can not pay for the printed folders. I propose to send the slides as one file and print nothing at all. That solution permit us to keep a reserve for the guest speaker. Tell me what you think, because the university asks for the plan until Friday.

Best wishes,
Camille
